## Xi Jinping, 2024, `1B.1` research note

I searched broadly with multiple formulations and kept to primary / highly credible sources. Best-supported conclusion: **Xi’s 2024 record contains strong declaratory evidence for nuclear-risk reduction, but also substantial counterevidence from nuclear modernization and coercive military behavior.** The pro-reduction evidence is mostly rhetoric and policy statements, not a verified operational rollback.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports reduction | [No-first-use of Nuclear Weapons Initiative](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html | Official Chinese nuclear policy paper states that Xi “re-affirmed” nuclear weapons cannot be used and nuclear war must not be fought, and that China supports no-first-use and a mutual no-first-use treaty. This is the clearest 2024 pro-risk-reduction evidence. | `1B.1` |
| Supports reduction | [Wang Yi Elaborates on China's Position on Ukraine Crisis](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-02-18 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zyxw/202405/t20240530_11332760.html | Wang Yi attributed to Xi the position that nuclear weapons must not be used and nuclear wars must not be fought, and said China should protect nuclear materials and facilities while pursuing a peaceful settlement of the Ukraine crisis. This supports a risk-reduction reading, though it is still declaratory. | `1B.1` |
| Supports reduction | [Maintaining Global Strategic Stability, Reducing Risks of Nuclear Conflicts](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-12 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/gjhdq_665435/3376_665447/3432_664920/3435_664926/202406/t20240612_11428155.html | China urged all nuclear-weapon states to diminish the role of nuclear weapons, avoid pre-emptive or launch-on-warning doctrines, and avoid actions that would spur arms races. This is indirect evidence for risk reduction, but it is not a direct Xi appearance. | `1B.1` |
| Cuts against reduction | [Role of nuclear weapons grows as geopolitical relations deteriorate—new SIPRI Yearbook out now](https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now) | SIPRI | 2024-06-17 | https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now | SIPRI reported China’s estimated arsenal rising from 410 warheads in Jan. 2023 to 500 in Jan. 2024 and said China may be deploying a small number of warheads on missiles during peacetime. That is strong evidence against a simple “risk reduction” interpretation. | `1B.1` |
| Cuts against reduction | [Senior Defense Official Briefs on 2024 China Military Power Report](https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/) | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-12-18 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/ | DoD said the PRC had surpassed 600 operational nuclear warheads by mid-2024 and was continuing a rapid nuclear buildup. That points toward expanded coercive leverage and strategic modernization, not de-escalation. | `1B.1` |
| Cuts against reduction | [PLA conducts joint military drills surrounding Taiwan Island](https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html) | PRC Ministry of National Defense / Xinhua | 2024-05-23 | https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html | Official PLA announcement described drills around Taiwan involving combat-readiness patrols, precision strikes, and a “stern warning” to Taiwan independence forces. This is not nuclear escalation per se, but it increases existential-risk pressure in a major-power flashpoint. | `1B.1` |

### Bottom line

- **Best case for `1B.1`:** Xi’s 2024 public line repeatedly favored no-first-use, “nuclear war must not be fought,” and strategic-stability / arms-control language.
- **Best case against `1B.1`:** China also kept expanding its nuclear arsenal and conducted coercive Taiwan drills, which are more consistent with leverage and deterrence pressure than with reducing existential risk.
- **Overall read:** I would treat 2024 as **mixed but not strongly pro-reduction**. The record shows **risk-reduction rhetoric**, but the material actions and force posture still point to **continued escalation capacity**.

### Search gap

I did **not** find a 2024 source showing Xi personally launched a concrete, verifiable de-escalation step such as a new arms-control agreement, force rollback, or transparency measure. The strongest pro-reduction evidence is declaratory and policy-oriented, not operational.
